title: What are the common factors of each group?
description: Four groups of numbers each need their common factors. Listing the factors of every number and keeping those in every list gives the answer, and a check puts some factors back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the common factors are the factors that appear in every list. Watch for students who leave out one.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q4, p.111
video_script.why: The child lists the factors of every number in a group and keeps those in every list, four times over.
video_script.substitution: List the factors of each number and keep those in every list.
video_script.anchor: four groups of numbers, each with factor lists side by side
video_script.payoff_line: The common factors are one, two and four, or one and five

final_answer.spoken: the common factors are one, two and four, or one and five

video_script.design: One idea: the common factors are the factors in every list. Same method as the book example: list the factors of each number and keep the shared ones.

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A factor that lands on every number in a group is called a common factor.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the factors in every list of each group.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, twenty and twenty eight. The factors of twenty are one, two, four, five, ten and twenty.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The factors of twenty eight are one, two, four, seven, fourteen and twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both lists have one, two and four.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, thirty five and fifty. Thirty five has factors one, five, seven and thirty five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Fifty has factors one, two, five, ten, twenty five and fifty.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both lists have one and five.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, four, eight and twelve. Four has factors one, two and four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Eight has factors one, two, four and eight.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Twelve has factors one, two, three, four, six and twelve.
<bookmark mark='all'/>All three lists have one, two and four.

<bookmark mark='b'/>Five times seven is thirty five, and five times ten is fifty.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Four times three is twelve, and five times five is twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) 1, 2, 4; (b) 1, 5; (c) 1, 2, 4; (d) 1, 5; the common factors are 1, 2, 4 or 1, 5

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The common factors are one, two and four, or one and five.
